messages:
matt: kicking off a config-only deploy (no model changes) — routing and batch limits. Canary 10% for 15m. I'll monitor latency and error-rate. @alice @sara FYI.

deploy-bot: started canary 6790012345 for config: route_policy=dynamic-prefer-low-latency, canary_pct=10, canary_window=15m

alice: thanks. which tenants are in the canary?

matt: tenants tagged 'canary-10'. mainly internal + a few low-traffic customers.

sara: watching p50/p95 and 5xx. will ping if p95 > 600ms or 5xx > 0.5%

tilly: any limits changed? need to know fallback plan if qps spikes.

matt: reduced per-tenant qps to 40 (from 60), introduced a soft rate floor, and lowered batch ttl. config snippet:
```
limits:
  tenant_max_qps: 40
  tenant_burst: 80
batching:
  max_batch_size: 24
  batch_ttl_ms: 100
routing:
  policy: dynamic-prefer-low-latency
timeouts:
  inference_ms: 3200
```

alice: ok. reduce batch_ttl looks risky for cost but should lower latency. monitor token throughput.

sara: spotting a slight uptick in tails at minute 4 — p95 moved from 380ms -> 520ms, 5xx still 0.2%

matt: noted. keep an eye. not a blocker yet.

tilly: recommend setting a canary pin in case we need a fast rollback: pin current running model version and route policy. put rollback playbook in the thread.

matt: adding quick rollback steps:
- unpin config: revert to previous routing + batch_ttl=160
- scale canary down to 0% via deploy-bot
- if 5xx > 1% or p95 > 800ms after revert, escalate to oncall

deploy-bot: canary update: 10% -> 10% (no change) at 6790012380

sara: at minute 9 p95 is back to 410ms, 5xx steady 0.25%. I'm comfortable to continue to 25% at 15m mark unless anything changes.

alice: +1. please post when you increase canary.

matt: OK bumping to 25% in 5m if steady. tagging @ops for awareness :bell: 

deploy-bot: scheduled canary ramp to 25% at 6790012445

matt: thanks team — will watch dashboard and post final status here.
